F.heading: ## F. Native targets & rendering — NEW SECTION

items.title:
NEW — RETIRE the parent-method forms `View::when` / `View::swap` (and `View::swap_split`, the split recognizer's retarget twin) in favour of the free `when` / `swap` of `std::ui` that A85 shipped in Order 35: `
{swap(value, \|x\| match x { Some(_) => "Exists", None => "Empty" })}{when(condition, \|\| "Is true")}
`. The methods are one-line sugar (`self.child(Conditional { .. })` / `self.child(Swap { .. })`) kept in lockstep across the browser and process layers; inside their own `impl` block they SHADOW the free function of the same name (which is why `split_route` exists under a third name and why the methods build the literal instead of calling the value form), and `chunks.rs` recognizes BOTH spellings of `swap` (lines 102/105 and 243/247) — one spelling halves it. BREAKING: the rewrite is mechanical, `parent.swap(s, r)` → `parent.child(swap(s, r))` or `{swap(s, r)}` in a child hole; census on 9b22ec36: kolt 6 `.swap` + 1 `.when` (theme.vl:270, views.vl:86/114/158/162/394, overlay.vl:502), std 0 live sites (router.vl:9 and ui.vl doc lines only), docs 7/6, examples 2/3, vilan-core tests 24/6, vilan-cli tests 11/9 (the `.when(` counts include `Style::when`, which STAYS). The owner's example spells `swap`/`when` BARE, so the `std::web` prelude gains the five slot functions (`when`, `swap`, `each`, `each_values`, `each_by`) beside `View`/`view`
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-14): 'File an item to replace `View.swap` and `View.when` with top-level `swap` and `when` functions'. OWNER QUESTIONS: (1) the `bind_each` / `bind_each_values` / `bind_each_by` trio is the same sugar over `each*` — retire them in the same order (rec: yes, one breaking order for all six, one migration note)?; (2) the path: pre-beta hard removal with an editor quick fix 'Use the value form' that rewrites the call (rec), or a `[deprecated]` window (`deprecation.md`)?
items.body: std: delete `View::when`/`View::swap`/`View::swap_split` in browser/ui.vl (411, 441, 589) and process/ui.vl (300, 316); fold `split_route` back into the free `swap_split` once nothing shadows it; the free forms' doc lines stop saying 'the value form of `View::swap`'. Compiler: `chunks.rs` recognizes the free `swap` only (`view_method(program, "swap")` arms go; the retarget pair becomes `std_free_function` only); B268's note at ui.vl:965 updates. Prelude: web.vl `export import pkg::ui::{ when, swap, each, each_values, each_by };` (E145's rule 0 then fades an explicit import of them — fine). Editor: a quick fix on the removed method ('no method `swap` on `View` — write `child(swap(..))` or `{swap(..)}`') via the curated-rule steer, rewriting in place. Estate: docs 7+6 sites, examples 2+3, tests 24+6 / 11+9 rewritten; kolt's 7 sites at the owner's word (views.vl:158's route swap becomes `{swap(get_route(), \|route\| match route { .. })}` with the inner `.swap` at :162 wrapped the same way — every arm then yields a `View` as today). Pins: the method form is refused with the steer; the free form in a child hole places at the anchor (A85's pins); the split recognizer still retargets a recognized `swap` VALUE; goldens for the split fixtures regenerate over the merged tree.

items.title: NEW — `SignalCell` (and `Owner`) off `Shared` boxes and onto `Rc` or OWNER-ATTACHED arena `Handle`s — the necessary step for native apps with native code and NO garbage collector (F1). Today `SignalCell<T> { value: Shared<T>, subscribers: Shared<List<Subscriber>>, identity }` and `Owner { cleanups: Shared<..>, disposed: Shared<bool> }`; `Shared` is a compiler primitive (`external struct`, `primitive_struct_ids` 'Shared', 8 analyzer sites) whose doc says 'reference-counted' but whose JS backing is a plain object box the HOST GC reclaims — nothing counts, cycles (cell ↔ subscriber closures capturing cells) are the GC's problem, and a disposed owner's cells stay readable forever. Neither property survives a native backend. Two candidate representations, to be DECIDED in a paper: (a) a real `Rc<T>` — counted box with deterministic drop (`destruction.md`, `drop.vl`), cycles broken by the owner's disposal or by `Weak` (C1, OPEN); (b) owner-attached `Arena` + `Handle` (std::arena already exists; the owner holds the arena, a cell is `Handle<Slot<T>>` + its owner, disposal frees the arena wholesale — no counting, no cycles, and a stale handle reads `None` instead of a ghost value, which is a BEHAVIOUR change from today for a cell that escapes its owner: module-level cells, `std::memo` caches, rpc mirrors, `Task` results). Blast radius: reactive.vl 47 `Shared` mentions, 13 std files use `Shared`, kolt 4 (store, lib/input_system, lib/overlay, lib/rotary)
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-14): 'change SignalCells from `Shared` boxes to `Rc` or arena `Handle`s (handles attached to owner). This is a necessary step to support native apps with native code (no garbage collector)'. Companion of F1; C1 (`Weak<T>`) is the other brick if (a) wins
items.body: Paper first (`proposal/signal-cell-representation.md` or a section of `memory-management.md`): (1) census every `Shared` use in std and kolt and classify each — owner-scoped (dies with a boundary), root-scoped (module-level, lives for the program), escaping (handed across owners: memo caches, rpc mirrors, `Task`); (2) the two representations against that census, with the JS backend as the FIRST target — an `Rc` on JS is a box whose counts are no-ops, an arena handle on JS is two integers plus a lookup, so either lands and is verified on JS (leak-soak.md's harness, `heap_cycles.js`) before any native backend exists; (3) the semantics of a read after the owner's disposal (today: the ghost value; arena: `None`/refusal; Rc: the value while any holder lives) and what `ambient-owner.md`'s `owner_scope` context guarantees; (4) subscriber lists — the cell → subscriber → closure → cell cycle is the one that forces `Weak` or the arena; (5) `Owner` itself (its `cleanups`/`disposed` boxes) and `Signal`/`Memo`/`RemoteSource`/`Task` in the same pass; (6) the `[derive(Wire)]` identity stamp (A92) survives either. Decide, then slice: representation type + std's reactive core on it + the JS pins green + kolt unchanged at the surface. Not before the paper: no `Shared` deletion — `Shared` stays for genuinely diffuse ownership (its own doc's case) and gains real counting under a native backend.

items.title: NEW — DISCUSSION: building GPU-RENDERED NATIVE APPS in vilan. Today the build model is `Target` = `Backend` + `Platform` (platform-model.md, implemented 2026-06-23) with ONE backend (the JS emitter) and the browser/node/deno/bun platforms; `std::ui` has two layers behind one public surface (browser = live DOM, process = SSR string tree — the precedent for a third). A native app needs FOUR things the project has none of: (1) a native BACKEND — emit Rust (rustc does codegen; vilan's affine moves, borrows and `own` map onto ownership) vs C vs wasm-in-a-host vs an interpreter; (2) memory without a GC — C14 (cells on Rc/owner arenas), real counting for `Shared`, closure captures (`capture-clones.md`), strings/lists with owners, `destruction.md`'s drops actually running; (3) a RENDER LAYER — a third `std::ui` twin building a retained scene tree rendered by a GPU renderer (wgpu + vello-class 2D, text shaping, a flexbox-class layout engine such as taffy) with `Style` mapped onto it (A95 conditions: `hover()`/`active()` become hit-test state, `media`/`sm..xl` become window queries, the `css` block a native style resolver) and events/input/windowing (winit-class); (4) std's platform layers (`[library.layer]`, `PlatformPattern`) admitting a `native` platform and the coloring rules deciding what a native entry may reach (no `std::dom`, no `fetch` shaped as the browser's). Prior art to measure against: Dioxus/Blitz (HTML+CSS semantics, vello-rendered), Makepad, Slint, GPUI (Zed), Flutter (Impeller)
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-09-14): 'File an item to discuss support for building GPU-rendered native apps'. OWNER QUESTIONS before a paper: (1) which backend — emitting Rust is the shortest path to a real binary and reuses the ecosystem (wgpu, winit, taffy, cosmic-text) but makes rustc a toolchain dependency; (2) scope — desktop first (Windows/Linux/macOS), mobile later?; (3) is the UI surface the DOM-shaped `View` (so kolt's views compile unchanged onto the native layer, the SSR precedent) or a new retained-tree API?; (4) does 'native app' mean client-only, or client + server in one process (the rpc runtime in-process)?; (5) sequencing — C14 first (verifiable on JS), then a backend probe (hand-translate one small vilan program to Rust and list what the emitter must know), then the render layer
items.body: Deliverable: a paper `proposal/native-apps.md` — the four pillars above as slices with a dependency order (C14 → backend probe → minimal native platform in the build model → render layer over a scene tree → style mapping → input/windowing), each slice's exit test (a `fun main()` printing to stdout as a native binary; a window with one styled `<div>`; kolt's sidebar rendered natively), a cost estimate per slice, and the ruling questions. The backend probe is the cheap first move: translate a 50-line vilan program (structs, a closure, a `List`, a `Signal`) to Rust by hand and enumerate the runtime the emitter needs (`List`/`Map`/`str` representations, closures as boxed `Fn` with captures, the reactive core on C14's representation). Cross-links: C14, C1, A95 (conditions map onto hit-test state), platform-model.md, platform-coloring.md, ssr.md/process.md (the second-layer precedent), memory-management.md, destruction.md, capture-clones.md. Not in scope until the paper is ruled: any compiler work.
